sections.title: Segment Mix
sections.subtitle: Intelligent Infrastructure (AI/datacenter/cloud) overtook the other two segments in FY2026

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Jabil Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Jabil Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Jabil Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Jabil Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Jabil Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Jabil Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Jabil Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Jabil Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Jabil Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
Jabil reports three segments: Regulated Industries (healthcare, automotive, packaging), Intelligent Infrastructure (AI/datacenter/cloud, networking, capital equipment) and Connected Living & Digital Commerce (mobility, retail/e-commerce hardware).

For Jabil Inc.: Intelligent Infrastructure grew from about 32% of revenue in FY2024 to roughly 50% in FY2026 (up 45% YoY in FY2026 alone) as hyperscalers ramp AI/data-center capex, while Connected Living & Digital Commerce has shrunk in absolute terms over the same period. This mix shift is the central re-rating question for the stock -- EMS margins on AI infrastructure differ from the legacy mix.

What to watch:

  • Whether Intelligent Infrastructure growth is broadening across customers or concentrated in one or two hyperscalers (see the customer-concentration KPI)
  • Regulated Industries' healthcare/packaging automation delays flagged by management
  • Whether the other two segments stabilise or keep shrinking as a share of the total

segmentIncome.title: Segment operating income
segmentIncome.content:
Segment income is each segment's operating income before corporate/unallocated costs -- it shows where Jabil's profit, not just revenue, is actually being made.

For Jabil Inc.: Intelligent Infrastructure's segment income roughly doubled FY2024-FY2026 (469 to 1,069) as AI-related volume scaled, while Connected Living & Digital Commerce's income fell alongside its revenue. Compare each segment's income against its revenue chart to see whether the AI mix shift is also margin-accretive, or just larger at a similar rate.

What to watch:

  • Intelligent Infrastructure's implied segment margin versus the other two
  • Corporate/unallocated costs eating into the sum of the three segments' income (the gap versus consolidated operating income)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Jabil Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
